# Data Source: stripe_commerce_product_catalog_import_v2

An import of a product catalog from an uploaded file, and its progress. Look one up by its `id`. The upload URL and the error file's download URL in `status_details` are sensitive.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_commerce_product_catalog_import_v2" "spring" {
  id = "pci_123"
}

output "import_status" {
  value = data.stripe_commerce_product_catalog_import_v2.spring.status
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the v2 commerce product catalog import to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `created` - The time this ProductCatalogImport was created.
* `feed_type` - The type of feed data being imported into the product catalog. Possible values: `inventory`, `pricing`, `product`, `promotion`.
* `livemode` - Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.
* `metadata` - Additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `mode` - The import strategy for handling existing catalog data. Possible values: `replace`, `upsert`.
* `status` - The current status of this ProductCatalogImport. Possible values: `awaiting_upload`, `failed`, `processing`, `succeeded`, `succeeded_with_errors`.
* `status_details` - Details about the current import status. See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `awaiting_upload` - Details when the import is awaiting file upload. See [`status_details.awaiting_upload`](#status_details.awaiting_upload) below.
* `failed` - Details when the import didn't complete. See [`status_details.failed`](#status_details.failed) below.
* `processing` - Details when the import is processing. See [`status_details.processing`](#status_details.processing) below.
* `succeeded` - Details when the import has succeeded. See [`status_details.succeeded`](#status_details.succeeded) below.
* `succeeded_with_errors` - Details when the import completed but some records failed to process. See [`status_details.succeeded_with_errors`](#status_details.succeeded_with_errors) below.

<a id="status_details.awaiting_upload"></a>
### `status_details.awaiting_upload`

The `status_details.awaiting_upload` attribute supports:

* `upload_url` - The pre-signed URL information for uploading the catalog file. See [`status_details.awaiting_upload.upload_url`](#status_details.awaiting_upload.upload_url) below.

<a id="status_details.awaiting_upload.upload_url"></a>
### `status_details.awaiting_upload.upload_url`

The `status_details.awaiting_upload.upload_url` attribute supports:

* `expires_at` - The timestamp when the upload URL expires.
* `url` - (Sensitive) The pre-signed URL for uploading the catalog file.

<a id="status_details.failed"></a>
### `status_details.failed`

The `status_details.failed` attribute supports:

* `code` - The error code for this product catalog processing failure. Possible values: `file_not_found`, `internal_error`, `invalid_file`.
* `failure_message` - A message explaining why the import failed.
* `type` - The error type for this product catalog processing failure. Possible values: `cannot_proceed`, `transient_failure`.

<a id="status_details.processing"></a>
### `status_details.processing`

The `status_details.processing` attribute supports:

* `error_count` - The number of records that failed to process so far.
* `success_count` - The number of records processed so far.

<a id="status_details.succeeded"></a>
### `status_details.succeeded`

The `status_details.succeeded` attribute supports:

* `success_count` - The total number of records processed.

<a id="status_details.succeeded_with_errors"></a>
### `status_details.succeeded_with_errors`

The `status_details.succeeded_with_errors` attribute supports:

* `error_count` - The total number of records that failed to process.
* `error_file` - A file containing details about all errors that occurred. See [`status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file`](#status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file) below.
* `samples` - A sample of errors that occurred during processing. See [`status_details.succeeded_with_errors.samples`](#status_details.succeeded_with_errors.samples) below.
* `success_count` - The total number of records processed.

<a id="status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file"></a>
### `status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file`

The `status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file` attribute supports:

* `content_type` - The MIME type of the error file.
* `download_url` - The pre-signed URL information for downloading the error file. See [`status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file.download_url`](#status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file.download_url) below.
* `size` - The size of the error file in bytes.

<a id="status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file.download_url"></a>
### `status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file.download_url`

The `status_details.succeeded_with_errors.error_file.download_url` attribute supports:

* `expires_at` - The timestamp when the download URL expires.
* `url` - (Sensitive) The pre-signed URL for downloading the error file.

<a id="status_details.succeeded_with_errors.samples"></a>
### `status_details.succeeded_with_errors.samples`

The `status_details.succeeded_with_errors.samples` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `error_message` - A description of what went wrong with this record.
* `field` - The name of the field that caused the error.
* `id` - The identifier of the record that failed to process.
* `row` - The row number in the import file where the error occurred.
